$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for @platos/adapter-outbox. One entry per ordering
invariant, envelope refusal, drain precondition and transaction guard in
the package, each carrying the file it lives in, the EXACT text that
implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED
cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
A guard nothing can turn red is a guard that is not there. Every entry
below was exercised before this adapter was proposed.
The store half of the outbox lives in packages/adapters/postgres-tenancy,
because ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM one home and this package may not hold
it. Its guards are in that package's mutations-outbox.json; the two
ledgers are separate because the two halves are separate packages with
separate suites, not because the outbox is two things.
This lives here rather than in README.md because that file is emitted by
scripts/arch/gen-v1-skeleton.mjs and byte-compared by `node
scripts/arch/gen-v1-skeleton.mjs --check`: adoption releases a project's
PLACEHOLDERS, never its scaffolding.
WIN-260 (M2.5) ADDS THE F-SERIES: the shutdown flush in src/flush.ts. It was
drafted at the process edge and scripts/arch/composition-root.mjs refused it
-- rule (C1) allows exactly ONE importer of an adapter package. The refusal
was right beyond the letter: everything the loop knows is outbox knowledge,
and a copy of it under apps/core-api would be a second place to get this
package's paging contract wrong.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills
and every one was VACUOUS: the context's dist/ had been cleaned, so every
suite failed to LOAD and would have 'died' against no mutation at all.
The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep unless it
is green, and classifies a module-load failure with no named failing case
as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
For one entry: replace its `from` with its `to` in the named file, run
confirm a NAMED case goes red. Then revert and confirm green.
NONE of these entries needs a database. That is the point of the split:
the identifier, the envelope and every refusal are decided above the
store, so they are falsifiable with no container at all.
THE F-SERIES NEEDS NO DATABASE EITHER, and four of its kills come from the
block that drives the REAL buildOutboxAdapter over the REAL
createInMemoryOutbox. Those are the ones worth reading: a compile-time
`Satisfies` compares two declarations, while F02 and F08 are killed by a loop
